habitat: Parties in broad-leaved and mixed woodland, in the middle and lower layers. Nomadic, and it sometimes appears in suburbia during droughts.
summary: A common resident. Pied, with a grey crown, a yellow eye and eye-wattle, and yellow legs. The identification line says the eye-wattles and legs are orange-yellow. The immature has a browner crown. Newman does not describe the voice. The Kemp name White Helmetshrike and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Retz’s Helmet-Shrike is black, with a red bill, eye-wattle and legs, and a white vent and tail tips.

head.pattern: Pied, with a grey crown. The identification line says orange-yellow eye-wattles and legs. The description says a yellow eye-wattle and yellow legs.

wings.pattern: Striking black-and-white wing markings. Flight looks slow, like a butterfly.

viewNotes.note: Pied, with a grey crown and a yellow eye.
Yellow eye and eye-wattle. The identification line says orange-yellow.
Slow, butterfly-like flight, with black-and-white wing markings.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the voice. The grade A file is a begging call from Popa Falls in Namibia. The filename is XC447081-White-crestedHelmetshrike_PopaFalls_Namibia_20180916_15h43.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It is also described as nomadic. The legs are orange-yellow on the identification line and yellow in the description, so no leg colour is stored. The voice is not described. The grade A recording is a begging call from Namibia. The Kemp name White Helmetshrike and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^14=16384 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 8192–32768.
